pathwayLabel: Certification by Endorsement — 10-Year Licensure History (Option C)
examName: None required under Option C — a passed licensing exam is only required if applying under Option A (NASCLA route) instead
steps: California is not one of Florida's reciprocal-agreement states (Louisiana, Mississippi, and North Carolina per the current CILB 32 form) — the $350 CILB 32 reciprocity form and fee do not apply to a California license.

Instead, apply via DBPR CILB 10, Certification by Endorsement (Section 489.115(3), Florida Statutes). The most broadly applicable route for a California contractor is Option C: hold a valid, current out-of-state license for at least 10 years, active now or within the last 2 years.

If your California license was earned via the NASCLA Commercial General Building Contractor exam instead, Option A may apply: pass Florida's Business and Finance exam and attest to passing an exam on the Florida Building Code — this route does not require 10 years of licensure.
Complete a board-approved 2-hour Florida Building Code course covering wind mitigation techniques (required for Certified General/Building/Residential/Roofing Contractor categories).
Submit electronic fingerprints, a FICO-derived credit report, and proof of satisfaction of any liens, judgments, or bankruptcy.
Pay the $350 Endorsement application fee to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation.
Await processing — DBPR does not publish a guaranteed timeline for this form; budget for several weeks to a few months.
notes: Fee and process confirmed directly from DBPR CILB 10 (Application for Certification by Endorsement, Section 489.115(3), F.S.), current version incorporated in Rule 61-35.010, F.A.C. (effective 2026-06-28, Ref-17718): $350 fee, three applicant options (A: passed a substantially equivalent exam, primarily used for NASCLA; B: license issued under substantially equivalent criteria, discretionary and described by DBPR's own form as 'very stringent and rarely approved'; C: 10+ years continuously active out-of-state license). California is not a reciprocal-agreement state (the separate CILB 32 reciprocity form, Ref-17723, lists only Louisiana, Mississippi, and North Carolina), so the $350 reciprocity fee and process do not apply here. Endorsement and reciprocity are distinct pathways: the current CILB 10 states 'For those applicants seeking licensure via reciprocity, please complete form CILB 32,' and CILB 32 cites Section 489.115(3)(c), F.S., as its basis. (An earlier CILB 10 revision said 'there are currently no reciprocal agreements in place' under an Option D; that wording is absent from the current form, which resolves the conflict previously flagged here.) Source note: DBPR's own domain (myfloridalicense.com) blocks automated fetches (403); the forms were retrieved from flrules.org, the Florida Administrative Register, as incorporated by reference under the F.A.C. rule. CORRECTION HISTORY (check the rule's effective date before editing this claim again): (a) Original claim: CILB 32 lists Louisiana, Mississippi, and North Carolina. (b) 2026-09-20: changed to Louisiana-only after an antiword extraction of a CILB 32 .doc found zero occurrences of 'Mississippi' or 'North Carolina'. That extraction apparently used an older copy of the form; which version it read was not recorded. (c) 2026-09-29: re-verified against the forms incorporated by reference in Rule 61-35.010, F.A.C. (latest effective date 2026-06-28; CILB 32 = Ref-17723, CILB 10 = Ref-17718), downloaded from flrules.org and extracted with antiword. The current CILB 32 names Louisiana, Mississippi, and North Carolina in its license-category checklist ('Louisiana or Mississippi' block and 'North Carolina' block, each General/Building/Residential only), restoring claim (a). The same re-verification corrected the CILB 10 endorsement fee from $354 to $350, and found the current CILB 10 no longer contains the earlier 'no reciprocal agreements in place' Option D wording. This record's conclusion (California doesn't qualify for reciprocity) is unaffected by any of these changes.
